Front: Why does LangChain memory exist; what LLM limitation does it work around?
Back: LLMs are stateless - each call is independent with no recollection of prior turns. Memory stores the conversation and re-injects it into the prompt every call (continuity = re-sending history). BufferWindow (last k) and Summary (compress) keep context/cost bounded.

Front: Prompt templates vs output parsers - what does each add?
Back: Templates: reusable, parameterized prompts (variables, few-shot). Output parsers are two-way: they inject format_instructions into the prompt to steer the model toward parseable output, then parse + validate the response into a dict/Pydantic object.

LLMChain = the atomic step (one prompt + LLM + optional parser). SequentialChain = several LLMChains wired output->input, with multiple named inputs/outputs. SimpleSequentialChain = the single-input/single-output linear version.

An LLM classifies the input and dispatches it to the best specialized destination chain (each with its own prompt/model), with a default fallback chain for unmatched queries. The learned version of mixture-of-experts gating.

Front: The RAG document-Q&A pipeline (PDF to grounded answer)?
Back: load (PyPDFLoader) -> split (RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter, overlapping chunks) -> embed (chunk -> vector) -> store (FAISS index) -> retrieve (embed question, similarity search, top-k) -> generate (stuff chunks into the prompt, LLM answers grounded in them). Steps 1-4 once (index); 5-6 per query. RetrievalQA / ConversationalRetrievalChain with memory.

Front: Retrieval chain types: stuff vs map_reduce vs refine vs map_rerank?
Back: How to combine retrieved chunks THROUGH the LLM (retrieval already happened). stuff = all chunks in one call (simplest; breaks past context window). map_reduce = LLM per chunk then combine (scales, more calls). refine = iterative answer + next chunk (slow). map_rerank = per-chunk answer + confidence, take highest.

Front: How does the retriever decide which chunks are relevant?
Back: Each chunk has one embedding vector; the question is embedded too; compare question vector to chunk vectors by cosine similarity and return the top-k nearest. It is semantic (meaning) matching, not keyword. (RAGAS context recall catches when the right chunk is worded too differently to retrieve.)

Front: What does wrapping an LLM in an agent add over a fixed chain?
Back: A reasoning/decision loop (ReAct: reason -> act -> observe -> repeat) plus tools. Control flow is dynamic - the LLM chooses which tools to call and when to stop - vs a chain's fixed predetermined path. More capable but less predictable and harder to eval.
